findings.text: — §1 now requires `test_matched_policy_rebuilds_from_frozen_scores_and_receipts` to run without skipping "from inputs committed in the repository", but those inputs are unrecoverable: the test reads two absolute paths into the reckon run store (`imas_codex/standard_names/review/cascade_calibration.py:34-41`), both run directories are gone from disk, and §1's own node evidence records "Neither directory exists any more … This node cannot restore them: they are outside its write scope and outside the repository" (`docs/evidence/fragments/sn-pipeline-hygiene/sph-red-other.html:97-103`). The clause states an outcome whose only named source does not exist, so the node dispatched on it must decide unaided whether to re-derive the receipts — and a re-derivation changes the calibrated cutoffs, because the test asserts `build() == json.loads(THRESHOLDS_PATH.read_text())` against the committed `cascade_thresholds.json`, so new receipts force a regenerated thresholds artifact and silently move a shipped calibration the plan never mentions changing. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: without saying whether the receipts are re-derived (and that the shipped thresholds are then regenerated) or the id is dropped, the §1 node either engages unbounded LLM spend to reproduce deleted run outputs or lands a regenerated production calibration under a section whose stated purpose is test hygiene.

— the opening sentence still says the thirteen "failed at every base and head measured on 2026-11-11, including both arms of the last landing", while §1's own two arm comments record the gap-rules head at `1 failed / 8654 passed` on 2026-11-11 and seven of these ids green there (`plan.html:107`, `:110`), so "every head" is false for the heads measured that day. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: no — REASON: the sentence immediately after states the 2026-11-12 state (twelve pass, one skips), which is what a dispatched node acts on; the historical account is loose about which heads were measured, not about the work remaining.

rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §1's new done-when clause requires the cascade-calibration id to run "from inputs committed in the repository", but the section's own cited evidence records that the two receipt inputs no longer exist anywhere and cannot be restored inside the node's scope.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §1 carries one deliverable: the thirteen named test ids are either repaired or owned, with no second subsystem in the section.
